s479.lawyer_check: to be checked by a lawyer
s479.not_automatic: Release is not automatic. The jail superintendent must apply to the court (the person or their lawyer can also apply), and the court decides.
s479.reason.death_or_life: This offence can be punished with death or life imprisonment, so Section 479 does not apply. Ordinary bail can still be sought.
s479.reason.table_no: The sentence table says Section 479 does not apply to this offence.
s479.reason.other_cases: More than one case is pending, so Section 479 release is not available (Section 479(2)). Ordinary bail can still be sought.
s479.reason.many_sections: More than one section is charged. Section 479(2) may bar release, so these dates are to be checked by a lawyer.
s479.reason.question: This question is not answered yet: "{question}" The maximum term may be different, so these dates are to be checked by a lawyer.
s479.reason.table_check: The sentence table flags this offence for checking{notes}. These dates are to be checked by a lawyer.
s479.reason.delay: {days} days of delay caused by the accused are not counted, so both dates move later by that many days.
s479.max.no_date_same: The offence date is not given, but the IPC and BNS maximums are the same.
s479.max.no_date_differs: The offence date is not given. The maximum is different under the IPC (offences before 1 July 2024), so the dates are to be checked by a lawyer.
s479.max.after_july: The offence happened on or after 1 July 2024, so the BNS maximum is used: only offences committed before 1 July 2024 use the old IPC maximum.
s479.max.before_no_ipc: The offence happened before 1 July 2024, but our sentence table has no IPC maximum for this offence, so the BNS maximum is shown and the dates are to be checked by a lawyer.
s479.max.before_ipc: The offence happened before 1 July 2024, so the IPC maximum is used: Article 20(1) of the Constitution bars a heavier penalty than the law in force when the offence happened.
s479.max.bns_higher: (The BNS maximum, {months} months, is higher and does not apply.)
s479.note.convicted: Only for a person never convicted of any offence before.
s479.note.part_month: Part of a month is counted as 30 days; to be checked by a lawyer.
s479.error.delay_negative: Delay caused by the accused can't be negative.
s479.error.custody_after_today: The date custody began can't be after today's date.
s479.error.offence_after_custody: The offence date can't be after the date custody began.

home.lead: Lighting the way to legal aid.
home.sub: Agent Raahi turns a person's story into a checked case file, finds the route from official sources, and drafts the letters. A supervising lawyer approves every draft.
home.story_label: Tell the story in your own words (no names)
home.story_placeholder: For example: The employer has not paid the worker for three months…
home.how_sub: Five stages, with a person in charge at every one.
home.how1_p: The volunteer types or speaks the story. Phone numbers, Aadhaar numbers and email addresses are removed first.
home.how2_p: When something is missing, we ask. When something is unclear, we don't guess.
home.how3_p: When the volunteer presses a button, the agent searches official websites and drafts the case summary, the letter and the legal aid application.
home.how4_p: A supervising lawyer approves, edits or sends back every draft and every research point. No one approves their own work.
home.today_1: Notes on paper or in chat messages
home.today_2: Dates and eligibility worked out by hand
home.today_4: Little record of who checked what
home.raahi_1: A structured summary, by role, never by name
home.raahi_2: Section 479 dates and eligibility by tested rule-based code
home.raahi_3: Drafts filled from templates, checked by a supervising lawyer
home.raahi_4: An audit record of every step
home.safe1_p: Nothing is sent or filed until the supervising lawyer approves it. No one can approve their own work.
home.safe2_t: Every legal point has a source.
home.safe2_p: Points come from our verified files or from official websites. Anything not yet checked is labelled until the supervisor approves it.
home.safe3_p: Phone and Aadhaar numbers are removed before the AI sees anything. The person's story is never stored, and volunteer notes must not include names.
home.safe4_t: It stops when facts don't add up.
home.safe4_p: When information is missing or contradictory, the system flags the issue and requests clarification rather than drawing premature conclusions.
home.safe5_p: It never predicts outcomes, bail chances or risk, and never promises release or recovery.
home.safe6_p: Date calculations and eligibility checks follow predefined, tested rules.

whyq.label: Why this is asked:
whyq.person: The drafts and the free legal aid check need to know who the help is for (their role, never their name).
whyq.outcome: The letter must say what the person is asking for.
whyq.year: Without the year, the timeline and how long the problem has gone on cannot be worked out.
whyq.ai_default: The agent suggested this to fill a gap in the story. Skip it if it does not fit.
whyq.elig.in_custody: Anyone in custody qualifies for free legal aid whatever their income.
whyq.elig.woman: A woman qualifies for free legal aid whatever her income.
whyq.elig.under_18: A child (anyone under 18) qualifies for free legal aid whatever their income.
whyq.elig.sc_st: A member of a Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe qualifies for free legal aid whatever their income.
whyq.elig.disability: A person with a disability qualifies for free legal aid whatever their income.
whyq.elig.state: The income limit for free legal aid, and the offices to write to, differ from state to state.
whyq.elig.annual_income: If none of the other grounds applies, free legal aid depends on income, against the state's limit.
whyq.f.custody_began: The Section 479 dates are counted from the day custody began.
whyq.f.offence_date: Offences before 1 July 2024 come under the IPC, later ones under the BNS; the maximum sentence can differ.
whyq.f.section: The section decides the maximum sentence, which the Section 479 dates are worked out from.
whyq.f.never_convicted: The one-third date (release on a personal bond) is only for someone never convicted before.
whyq.f.other_cases_pending: Section 479 is not available when an investigation, inquiry or trial is pending for more than one offence, or in more than one case.
whyq.f.answer: The answer decides which maximum sentence applies.
whyq.f.delay_days_by_accused: Delay caused by the accused does not count towards the Section 479 time.
whyq.f.lawyer: If the person has no lawyer yet, a free legal aid application to the DLSA is drafted too.
